title: feat(agents): open agent databases through the selected engine

commit.messageHeadline: feat(agents): open agent databases through the selected engine
test(database): keep native SQLite fixtures explicit
fix(agents): carry engine selection through worker and search callers
test(agents): narrow native schema probe fixtures
fix(memory): keep engine selection behind the private host facade
fix(build): resolve wrapper inventory after rebase
fix(build): reconcile wrapper inventory with current main

Codex review: blocked before merge. ## What this changes This PR routes agent databases, transcripts, and agent auth storage through the database engine selected at boot. **Example:** Create agent main in a fresh state directory with database.engine set to postgres. - **Before:** The agent database still stores application rows in native SQLite. - **After:** Application rows use PostgreSQL while a local SQLite anchor retains physical identity. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Useful production-owner conformance coverage supports the design, but concrete PostgreSQL failures and incomplete existing-state compatibility prevent merge readiness. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | This maintainer-authored PR is outside the ordinary contributor proof gate; its PostgreSQL 17 conformance evidence exercises real agent owners, auth reads, persistence, and worker FIFO, but existing-state compatibility still needs a v2026.10.3 SQLite upgrade preserving auth and transcripts. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 4 actionable review findings remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Selecting PostgreSQL still leaves agent transcripts and agent auth data in SQLite. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction completes an existing engine contract and explicitly documents its experimental limits. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 5 items remain** Keep this PR open: the approved engine cutover is useful, but four reachable PostgreSQL failures block merging. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `b5e9fe28a2938e197fd09b45f4d54aefb115c048` ## Before merge - [ ] **Route Doctor ownership revalidation through the agent worker (P1)** - With PostgreSQL selected, any main-thread call requesting revalidateSchema bypasses the cached-metadata return and throws outside the existing inspection error handler. Doctor's stale-auth-order scanner makes exactly this request for existing agent auth databases, so reaching that inspection aborts the scan instead of returning ownership facts. Migrate those callers to asynchronous worker inspection before rejecting synchronous revalidation. - [ ] **Prepare local capability auth ownership in a worker (P2)** - prepareLocalCapabilityAccountSecrets calls this function on the main thread for local model, image, and audio execution. The new PostgreSQL branch calls openOpenClawAgentDatabaseReadOnly, which immediately asserts worker execution before even checking for a missing database. Consequently these commands throw before preparing credentials whenever PostgreSQL is selected. Use the existing asynchronous agent owner or prepared ownership facts. - [ ] **Port run-input visibility SQL to the selected engine (P2)** - This helper now accepts PostgreSQL connections, and the production history reader invokes it when resolving run-message visibility, but its projection still calls SQLite json_object and json_extract.
